chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja‘far (peace be upon him), who said:

One of you takes comfort from the oil, and water is more expansive than that. Shall I narrate to you the ablution of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)? I said, ‘Yes’. He said, ‘So he entered his hand into the vessel and did not wash his hand, but he took a palmful of water and poured it upon his face. Then he wiped its two sides until he had wiped all of it. Then he took another palmful with his right hand and poured it upon his left side, then washed with it his right arm. Then he took another palmful and washed with it his left arm. Then he wiped his head and his feet with whatever remained in his hand.’

key_terms.الدُّهْنِ: Oil or fat (used as a metaphor for comfort)
key_terms.جَانِبَيْهِ: Its two sides (referring to the face)
key_terms.كَفّاً: Palmful (a measure of water held in the hand)

ai.seo_question: What is the specific method of performing ablution (wudu) as demonstrated by the Messenger of Allah in this narration?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Prophetic practice of pouring water directly from the hand into the vessel without pre-washing, a detail often discussed in Shia fiqh regarding the sufficiency of water contact. It emphasizes the methodical application of water to the face, arms, head, and feet, reinforcing the ritual purity (taharah) described in Surah al-Ma'idah. The narration serves as a practical guide for believers to emulate the exact manner in which the Prophet performed wudu, ensuring the validity of their prayers.
